column3: “Lay down” is rendered “slept.”
NASB spells “Azaryahu.” The Hebrew has “king of Israel,” as NASB does.
“Excellent things” is rendered “precious things.”
“Arose over” is rendered “had taken over,” and “strengthened himself” as “made himself secure.” “Leaders” is rendered “rulers.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB uses parentheses.
“Said” is rendered “promised,” “descendants” as “sons,” and “all the days” as “forever.”
“From under the hand of Judah” is rendered “against the rule of Judah.”
NASB supplies “his.”
“From under the hand of Judah” is rendered “against Judah,” and “from under his hand” as “against his rule.”
“Made … prostitute themselves” is rendered “caused … to play the harlot,” and “thrust aside” as “led … astray.”
“A writing” is rendered “a letter,” and “ancestor” as “father.”
“The house of your father” is rendered “your own family.”
“Strike a great blow” is rendered “strike … with a great calamity,” and “property” as “possessions.”
“Great sicknesses” is rendered “severe sickness,” and “days to days” as “day by day.”
“On the hand of the Cushites” is rendered “who bordered the Ethiopians.”
“Broke into it” is rendered “invaded it.”
“Struck” is rendered “smote,” and “a sickness to there was not healing” as “an incurable sickness.”
“To days from days” is rendered “in the course of time,” and “harmful diseases” as “great pain.” “Burning” is rendered “fire.”
“With not desire” is rendered “with no one's regret,” and “graves” as “tombs.”
